summary_paragraph: A male patient with mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and a history of orthostatic hypotension was admitted for evaluation of hypotension and chest pain. He presented from cardiology clinic with systolic blood pressure as low as 85, presyncope, and self-resolving chest pressure. Initial workup ruled out acute myocardial infarction, with normal cardiac enzymes and EKGs showing only minimal changes. He was found to have acute kidney injury with creatinine rising from baseline 1.2 to 1.5, attributed to chronic dehydration from his mitochondrial disorder. He received IV fluids, which improved renal function to creatinine 1.1. His blood pressure medications—clonidine, diltiazem, and isosorbide mononitrate—were held due to symptomatic orthostasis and bradycardia. Metoprolol was reduced to 25 mg daily. Valsartan was continued. He was discharged home with plans to follow up for autonomic dysfunction and GI evaluation for malabsorption, with instructions to restart isosorbide mononitrate in clinic.
